question: Does the fresh C1 immediate heap proxy correspond to more observed V8 allocated-field bytes, or a different GC schedule, on the same no-history capture workload?
scope: New persistent November16 diagnostic only. Three fresh serial children: recovered baseline5d, freshly built C1, and baseline5d with a retained500000-element plain array planted in the capture interval. Exact package and Node identities join the new comparison plan. No C3 reconstruction or revalidation; no historical raw results are pooled.
workload: 1000 active nine-field rows,20 meaningful distinct field updates and untouched sentinel,20 direct whole source captures held live,21 exact expected requirement refs per capture. No packed history. Same production runtime mode as comparison; no browser/facade inference.
method: Invoke Node with --expose-gc --trace-gc-nvp. Four setImmediate-separated GCs precede ST_CAPTURE_BEGIN. Then perform20captures, optional planted array, ST_CAPTURE_END, one synchronous forced GC, ST_CAPTURE_AFTER_GC. Sum numeric allocated fields of trace GC lines between BEGIN and AFTER_GC; report event count/kind and whether an automatic GC occurred before END. Preserve fullstdout/stderr and exact markers. The interval includes fixed marker/harness overhead; these observed V8 fields are not a universal total-allocation or external-memory measure.
controls: Capture exact references/order/frozen-fresh identities and meaningful endpoints must pass. Planted array must remain live through forced GC and retain its500000values. Its observed interval allocated sum must exceed normal baseline by at least1500000bytes; otherwise allocation interpretation is not admitted. This threshold does not presume the engine's exact tagged-slot width. Require markers once/in order and at least one GC record after END. Never infer retained growth from immediate heap alone.
limits: One child per diagnostic arm, no distribution or timing claim. Tracing changes execution. Any GC-field interpretation is limited to this instrumented interval and separated from uninstrumented CPU/elapsed and heap. These fields do not recover previous children's automatic GC schedule. Stop/preserve an unexpected failure.
